title: DNA, Genes, Chromosomes, and Traits Review Test
description: Spaced review for use models to connect DNA, genes, chromosomes, proteins, and observable traits without reducing genetics to memorized vocabulary.

questions.prompt: Which phrase best summarizes the concept?
questions.questionText: Which phrase best summarizes the concept?
options: DNA is information that cells use in ways that can affect traits.
questions.correctAnswer: DNA is information that cells use in ways that can affect traits.
questions.explanation: This keeps information, cells, and traits connected.

questions.prompt: A model labels one section of DNA on a chromosome. What is that section?
questions.questionText: A model labels one section of DNA on a chromosome. What is that section?
questions.explanation: A gene is a DNA section.

questions.prompt: Which evidence best supports a gene-to-trait explanation?
questions.questionText: Which evidence best supports a gene-to-trait explanation?
options: The trait name is easy to spell.
Different gene versions lead to different protein activity and different pigment amounts.
The organism was observed after lunch.
questions.correctAnswer: Different gene versions lead to different protein activity and different pigment amounts.
questions.explanation: Evidence should connect information, cell process, and trait.

questions.prompt: A student says, "The trait is inside the chromosome." What correction is best?
questions.questionText: A student says, "The trait is inside the chromosome." What correction is best?
options: The chromosome stores DNA; the trait is observed in the organism.
questions.correctAnswer: The chromosome stores DNA; the trait is observed in the organism.
questions.explanation: Separate the information package from the observed result.

questions.prompt: Why can two environments produce different trait measurements in similar plants?
questions.questionText: Why can two environments produce different trait measurements in similar plants?
options: Environment can affect how traits are expressed.
questions.correctAnswer: Environment can affect how traits are expressed.
questions.explanation: Observed traits can depend on conditions.

options: trait -> no cell -> random word -> gene
DNA -> gene -> protein or cell process -> trait
questions.correctAnswer: DNA -> gene -> protein or cell process -> trait
questions.explanation: The chain connects the main levels.

questions.prompt: A table shows one gene version makes no working enzyme. What might happen?
questions.questionText: A table shows one gene version makes no working enzyme. What might happen?
options: A trait connected to that enzyme may be different.
questions.correctAnswer: A trait connected to that enzyme may be different.
questions.explanation: A cell-process change can affect related traits.

options: A gene may affect a trait, but the evidence should show how.
Any trait proves exactly one gene caused it.
DNA is never related to traits.
questions.correctAnswer: A gene may affect a trait, but the evidence should show how.
questions.explanation: Scientific explanations need mechanism and evidence.

questions.prompt: What does a chromosome do in this model?
questions.questionText: What does a chromosome do in this model?
options: organizes a long DNA molecule that contains genes
questions.correctAnswer: organizes a long DNA molecule that contains genes

options: What cell-process difference is connected to this gene version?
questions.correctAnswer: What cell-process difference is connected to this gene version?

questions.prompt: A diagram skips from gene directly to flower color. What should be added?
questions.questionText: A diagram skips from gene directly to flower color. What should be added?
options: a cell process such as pigment protein activity
questions.correctAnswer: a cell process such as pigment protein activity

options: Organisms can choose new inherited genes because they need a trait.
questions.correctAnswer: Organisms can choose new inherited genes because they need a trait.
questions.explanation: Inherited genetic information is not chosen by need.

questions.prompt: Which data pattern supports a real relationship?
questions.questionText: Which data pattern supports a real relationship?
options: The same gene version repeatedly matches the same protein activity pattern.
The same pen was used each day.
The graph has four grid lines.
questions.correctAnswer: The same gene version repeatedly matches the same protein activity pattern.

questions.prompt: Why is the word 'may' useful in gene-trait claims?
questions.questionText: Why is the word 'may' useful in gene-trait claims?
options: Many traits can involve several genes, cell processes, or environmental effects.
questions.correctAnswer: Many traits can involve several genes, cell processes, or environmental effects.
questions.explanation: Careful claims leave room for complexity.

questions.prompt: Which answer best transfers the idea to a new trait?
questions.questionText: Which answer best transfers the idea to a new trait?
options: Assume the color is the DNA.
For a seed coat trait, look for gene differences, cell-process differences, and seed coat evidence.
questions.correctAnswer: For a seed coat trait, look for gene differences, cell-process differences, and seed coat evidence.
questions.explanation: The same model can be used with a new trait.
